question:
Read the following passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Literacy is frequently described as the ____1____ upon which all other forms of learning are built. A person who can read and write is better equipped to access information, exercise legal rights and participate meaningfully in civic life. Recognising this, many countries have enshrined education as a fundamental right, obliging the state to provide free and compulsory schooling ____2____ children reach a certain age. Yet enrolment figures alone do not ____3____ genuine literacy; poorly resourced classrooms, overburdened teachers and high dropout rates can leave students technically enrolled but functionally unable to read with confidence. Girls, in particular, ____4____ historically excluded from schooling in many regions, and targeted measures remain necessary to close this gap. Only when literacy is treated as a right rather than a privilege ____5____ its transformative promise be fully realised.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. bedrock.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bedrock means the fundamental basis or foundation on which something else is built, fitting the phrase 'upon which all other forms of learning are built' (आधार / नींव).

◦ Example: Trust is the bedrock of any successful partnership.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 'ornament' means a decorative addition, and Option 3 'ceiling' refers to an upper limit or boundary — neither conveys the sense of a foundational base.

• Option 2 'shadow' suggests a faint trace or imitation, which does not fit the idea of something solid on which learning is built.

NOTE

• Words like 'bedrock', 'cornerstone' and 'foundation' are commonly used metaphorically to describe the essential basis of something important; look for this sense when a sentence mentions something 'built upon' another idea.

A person who can read and write is better equipped to access information, exercise legal rights and participate meaningfully in civic life. Recognising this, many countries have enshrined education as a fundamental right, obliging the state to provide free and compulsory schooling ____2____ children reach a certain age. Yet enrolment figures alone do not ____3____ genuine literacy; poorly resourced classrooms, overburdened teachers and high dropout rates can leave students technically enrolled but functionally unable to read with confidence. Girls, in particular, ____4____ historically excluded from schooling in many regions, and targeted measures remain necessary to close this gap. Only when literacy is treated as a right rather than a privilege ____5____ its transformative promise be fully realised.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. until.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Until indicates the point up to which an action continues, correctly showing that schooling is compulsory up to a certain age (जब तक).

◦ Example: The shop remains open until ten o'clock every night.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 'since' refers to a starting point in the past, and Option 3 'unless' introduces a negative condition, neither of which matches the intended meaning of a continuing duty up to a certain age.

• Option 2 'while' suggests simultaneous actions rather than a duration with an endpoint, which does not fit this context.

NOTE

• Use 'until' (or 'till') to indicate the endpoint of a continuous action or state, and reserve 'since' for a starting point in time.

Recognising this, many countries have enshrined education as a fundamental right, obliging the state to provide free and compulsory schooling ____2____ children reach a certain age. Yet enrolment figures alone do not ____3____ genuine literacy; poorly resourced classrooms, overburdened teachers and high dropout rates can leave students technically enrolled but functionally unable to read with confidence. Girls, in particular, ____4____ historically excluded from schooling in many regions, and targeted measures remain necessary to close this gap. Only when literacy is treated as a right rather than a privilege ____5____ its transformative promise be fully realised.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. guarantee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guarantee means to ensure or assure a certain outcome; the passage argues that mere enrolment does not ensure real literacy (सुनिश्चित करना).

◦ Example: A high score in one exam does not guarantee long-term success.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 'prevent' would mean enrolment stops literacy from happening, which contradicts the intended meaning.

• Option 2 'measure' and Option 4 'improve' shift the meaning away from the passage's point about assurance of outcome, making them contextually weaker choices.

NOTE

• When a sentence contrasts a visible statistic (like enrolment figures) with a deeper reality, words like 'guarantee' or 'ensure' are often the intended fit, showing that the statistic alone is not sufficient proof.

A person who can read and write is better equipped to access information, exercise legal rights and participate meaningfully in civic life. Recognising this, many countries have enshrined education as a fundamental right, obliging the state to provide free and compulsory schooling ____2____ children reach a certain age. Yet enrolment figures alone do not ____3____ genuine literacy; poorly resourced classrooms, overburdened teachers and high dropout rates can leave students technically enrolled but functionally unable to read with confidence. Girls, in particular, ____4____ historically excluded from schooling in many regions, and targeted measures remain necessary to close this gap. Only when literacy is treated as a right rather than a privilege ____5____ its transformative promise be fully realised.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. have been.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The present perfect passive 'have been excluded' correctly shows an action that began in the past and remains relevant to the present situation described in the passage (रही हैं).

◦ Example: Women have been underrepresented in this field for many years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 'are' describes only the present state without the historical continuity implied by 'historically'; Option 3 'had been' (past perfect) would require a specific past reference point, which is absent here.

• Option 2 'were being' (past continuous passive) incorrectly suggests a specific, ongoing past action rather than a pattern continuing to the present.

NOTE

• When a sentence contains a time marker like 'historically' that links the past to the present, the present perfect tense ('have/has been') is usually the most appropriate choice.

A person who can read and write is better equipped to access information, exercise legal rights and participate meaningfully in civic life. Recognising this, many countries have enshrined education as a fundamental right, obliging the state to provide free and compulsory schooling ____2____ children reach a certain age. Yet enrolment figures alone do not ____3____ genuine literacy; poorly resourced classrooms, overburdened teachers and high dropout rates can leave students technically enrolled but functionally unable to read with confidence. Girls, in particular, ____4____ historically excluded from schooling in many regions, and targeted measures remain necessary to close this gap. Only when literacy is treated as a right rather than a privilege ____5____ its transformative promise be fully realised.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. can.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the inverted structure beginning with 'Only when...', the modal 'can' correctly agrees with the present tense of 'is treated' and expresses the possibility that becomes available under that condition (सकना).

◦ Example: Only when the roots are strong can a tree withstand a storm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 'could' and Option 2 'might' imply a hypothetical or past possibility, which does not match the present tense condition set up by 'is treated'.

• Option 4 'should' expresses obligation or advice rather than capability, which does not fit the meaning of enabling a promise to be realised.

NOTE

• After a negative or restrictive phrase like 'Only when', 'Only if' or 'Never', the subject and auxiliary verb are inverted, and the auxiliary's tense must match the tense of the condition clause.

question:
Read the following passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The mounting volume of waste generated by modern lifestyles has turned disposal into one of the most pressing challenges facing cities today. Much of what is thrown away ____1____ decades to decompose, releasing pollutants into soil and groundwater long after it leaves our hands. Segregating waste ____2____ source, into biodegradable, recyclable and hazardous categories, remains one of the simplest yet most neglected steps households can take. When properly sorted, materials such as glass, metal and paper can be reprocessed ____3____ new products, easing pressure on landfills and conserving raw resources. Municipal authorities, meanwhile, are experimenting with composting units and waste-to-energy plants, though such initiatives often falter ____4____ public cooperation is weak or infrastructure is inadequate. Ultimately, meaningful change will depend less on technology than on a shift in everyday habits, ____5____ citizens learn to see waste not as something to be discarded thoughtlessly but as a resource to be managed responsibly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. takes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Takes is used with a duration of time to show how long a process requires, here how long waste requires to decompose (समय लगना).

◦ Example: It takes several years for plastic bottles to break down in landfills.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 'consumes' and Option 2 'spends' are typically used with a person or entity actively using time or resources, not with an inanimate process like decomposition.

• Option 4 'lasts' would mean the waste itself continues to exist for decades, which shifts the meaning slightly and does not fit as naturally with the infinitive 'to decompose' that follows.

NOTE

• The structure 'It takes + time + to + verb' is a common and fixed pattern for expressing duration; 'spend' and 'consume' are reserved for subjects who actively use time, like people.

Segregating waste ____2____ source, into biodegradable, recyclable and hazardous categories, remains one of the simplest yet most neglected steps households can take. When properly sorted, materials such as glass, metal and paper can be reprocessed ____3____ new products, easing pressure on landfills and conserving raw resources. Municipal authorities, meanwhile, are experimenting with composting units and waste-to-energy plants, though such initiatives often falter ____4____ public cooperation is weak or infrastructure is inadequate. Ultimately, meaningful change will depend less on technology than on a shift in everyday habits, ____5____ citizens learn to see waste not as something to be discarded thoughtlessly but as a resource to be managed responsibly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. at.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At source is a fixed idiomatic phrase meaning at the point of origin, commonly used with segregation or deduction of waste, tax, etc. (स्रोत पर).

◦ Example: Tax is deducted at source before the salary is credited.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 'from', 2 'by' and 4 'in' do not form the standard idiomatic phrase with 'source' in this context; only 'at source' is grammatically and idiomatically correct.

NOTE

• Learn fixed idiomatic phrases with prepositions as complete units, since substituting even a similar preposition often makes the phrase incorrect, e.g., 'at source', 'at hand', 'at large'.

When properly sorted, materials such as glass, metal and paper can be reprocessed ____3____ new products, easing pressure on landfills and conserving raw resources. Municipal authorities, meanwhile, are experimenting with composting units and waste-to-energy plants, though such initiatives often falter ____4____ public cooperation is weak or infrastructure is inadequate. Ultimately, meaningful change will depend less on technology than on a shift in everyday habits, ____5____ citizens learn to see waste not as something to be discarded thoughtlessly but as a resource to be managed responsibly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. into.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Reprocessed into shows the transformation of one material into a different form or product, correctly pairing with 'new products' (में बदलना).

◦ Example: Old newspapers can be reprocessed into fresh sheets of paper.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 'to' and Option 3 'as' do not fit the collocation 'reprocess something into something else'; Option 2 'for' would incorrectly suggest purpose rather than transformation.

NOTE

• Verbs describing transformation or conversion (turn, convert, reprocess, transform) are typically followed by 'into' when indicating the new resulting form.

The mounting volume of waste generated by modern lifestyles has turned disposal into one of the most pressing challenges facing cities today. Much of what is thrown away ____1____ decades to decompose, releasing pollutants into soil and groundwater long after it leaves our hands. Segregating waste ____2____ source, into biodegradable, recyclable and hazardous categories, remains one of the simplest yet most neglected steps households can take. When properly sorted, materials such as glass, metal and paper can be reprocessed ____3____ new products, easing pressure on landfills and conserving raw resources. Municipal authorities, meanwhile, are experimenting with composting units and waste-to-energy plants, though such initiatives often falter ____4____ public cooperation is weak or infrastructure is inadequate. Ultimately, meaningful change will depend less on technology than on a shift in everyday habits, ____5____ citizens learn to see waste not as something to be discarded thoughtlessly but as a resource to be managed responsibly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. where.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Where is used here to introduce a clause describing the circumstances or conditions under which initiatives falter, not a literal place (जहाँ / ऐसी स्थिति में जहाँ).

◦ Example: The plan works well where community support is strong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 'when' focuses on time rather than circumstance, making it a plausible but less precise fit than 'where' in this context.

• Options 1 'which' and 3 'that' cannot introduce this type of clause without a preceding preposition, making them grammatically incorrect here.

NOTE

• 'Where' can be used figuratively to mean 'in situations/cases in which', not only to refer to physical locations — a usage frequently tested in formal writing.

The mounting volume of waste generated by modern lifestyles has turned disposal into one of the most pressing challenges facing cities today. Much of what is thrown away ____1____ decades to decompose, releasing pollutants into soil and groundwater long after it leaves our hands. Segregating waste ____2____ source, into biodegradable, recyclable and hazardous categories, remains one of the simplest yet most neglected steps households can take. When properly sorted, materials such as glass, metal and paper can be reprocessed ____3____ new products, easing pressure on landfills and conserving raw resources. Municipal authorities, meanwhile, are experimenting with composting units and waste-to-energy plants, though such initiatives often falter ____4____ public cooperation is weak or infrastructure is inadequate. Ultimately, meaningful change will depend less on technology than on a shift in everyday habits, ____5____ citizens learn to see waste not as something to be discarded thoughtlessly but as a resource to be managed responsibly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. whereby.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Whereby is a formal relative adverb meaning 'by which' or 'through which', linking the shift in habits to the resulting change in how citizens view waste (जिसके द्वारा).

◦ Example: The committee proposed a system whereby complaints could be tracked online.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 'whereas' means 'while, in contrast', introducing a contrast rather than a mechanism, which does not fit the sentence's logic.

• Option 2 'hereby' means 'by this present action or document' and Option 3 'wherefore' means 'for what reason', neither of which fits the intended meaning of describing a process.

NOTE

• 'Whereby' is commonly used in formal writing to mean 'by means of which', linking an abstract process or system to its effect — do not confuse it with 'whereas' (contrast) or 'wherefore' (reason).
